questions.q: Which of the following is the highest level of cognitive ability according to Bloom's Taxonomy?
questions.exp: In the revised Bloom's Taxonomy (2001), 'Creating' (synthesis) is considered the highest level of cognitive learning.

questions.q: What is the main objective of formative evaluation?
opts: To promote students to the next class
questions.exp: Formative evaluation is conducted during the teaching-learning process to provide continuous feedback and improve student learning.

questions.q: Which level of teaching involves the highest order of thinking skills?
questions.exp: Reflective level is the highest level of teaching. It is highly thoughtful, problem-centric, and requires maximum cognitive involvement.

questions.q: SWAYAM is an acronym that stands for:
opts: Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds
Study World of Action-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds
Study Webs of Active-Learning for Youth Awareness Models
Social Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds
questions.exp: SWAYAM stands for Study Webs of Active-Learning for Young Aspiring Minds. It is an Indian MOOC platform.

questions.q: Who among the following propounded the 'Heuristic Method' of teaching?
questions.exp: The Heuristic method was advocated by Professor H.E. Armstrong. 'Heurisko' means 'I find out', making it a discovery-based method.

questions.q: Which of the following assessments is typically used to identify the specific learning difficulties of a student?
questions.exp: Diagnostic assessment is used to identify students' specific strengths, weaknesses, knowledge, and skills prior to instruction.

questions.q: A teacher gives a lot of positive and negative examples to support his / her presentations in the classroom. This will be related to which level of teaching?
questions.exp: Giving positive and negative examples helps students understand relationships and concepts, which falls under the Understanding Level of teaching.

questions.q: Micro-teaching is most effective for:
questions.exp: Micro-teaching is a teacher training technique used during preparation to master specific teaching skills in a scaled-down teaching environment.

questions.q: Which among the following is a learner-centered teaching method?
questions.exp: The Project method is learner-centered. Students solve practical problems over a period of days or weeks under the teacher's guidance.

questions.q: Which educational psychologist introduced the 'Cone of Experience' to explain the effectiveness of different learning media?
questions.exp: Edgar Dale introduced the Cone of Experience, which shows that learners retain more information by what they 'do' compared to what they 'hear' or 'read'.

questions.q: The Choice Based Credit System (CBCS) provides a choice for students to select from the prescribed courses. Which of these is NOT a course type in CBCS?
questions.exp: CBCS includes Core, Elective, and Foundation (Ability Enhancement) courses. 'Diagnostic Course' is not a category.

questions.q: In a Norm-Referenced Testing (NRT) model, a student's performance is compared with:
questions.exp: Norm-Referenced Tests (NRT) compare a student's performance against the performance of a peer group (the norm).

questions.q: Which teaching maxim suggests that a teacher should first teach the whole lesson and then break it down into parts?
questions.exp: The maxim 'Whole to Part' is based on Gestalt psychology, which states that we first perceive an object as a whole and then notice its parts.

questions.q: What is a 'Flipped Classroom'?
opts: A classroom where seats are arranged in a circle
Students learn instructional content at home and do activities/homework in class
A classroom entirely managed by students
Teacher teaches from the back of the classroom
questions.exp: In a flipped classroom, traditional homework is done in class, and instructional content (like video lectures) is consumed at home.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of an asynchronous learning tool?
questions.exp: Asynchronous learning happens on the student's schedule (not in real-time). Email and recorded videos are examples of this.

questions.q: Which philosophy of education emphasizes the role of the environment in shaping human behavior?
questions.exp: Behaviorism, associated with psychologists like Watson and Skinner, emphasizes that learning is a conditioning process shaped by the environment.

questions.q: The concept of 'Zone of Proximal Development' (ZPD) was given by:
questions.exp: Lev Vygotsky introduced ZPD, which is the difference between what a learner can do without help and what they can do with guidance.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a 'Key Behavior' contributing to effective teaching?
questions.exp: According to Gary Borich, Instructional Variety is one of the 5 key behaviors for effective teaching (along with Lesson clarity, Teacher task orientation, Engagement in learning process, and Student success rate).

questions.q: Which characteristic best defines an 'Adult Learner' (Andragogy)?
opts: Dependent on the teacher for all learning
Prefers subject-centered learning rather than problem-centered
questions.exp: Adult learners (Andragogy) are typically self-directed, intrinsically motivated, and use their life experiences as a resource for learning.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a 'Rubric' in educational assessment?
opts: To provide a scoring guide with specific criteria for grading
To design the classroom seating arrangement
questions.exp: A rubric is an evaluation tool or set of guidelines used to promote the consistent application of learning expectations, objectives, or standards.
